observations.authority_scope: Official provincial thematic cartographic usage supports bounded associations. The publication does not establish a formal naming-registry decision, current surveyed shoreline or exact named-water boundary.
observations.own_observations: Highrock Lake and Nelson Lake are distinct supported associations in the first selected ring, whose northern arm remains unnamed. Sisipuk Lake is supported for the eastern Manitoba basin of the second ring, with the western portion outside provincial map coverage. Granville Lake is supported for the third ring's main basin and northeastern arm; its southern prong follows the Laurie-labelled corridor with exact named-water scope unresolved. Suwannee and Costello proximity does not establish additional selected components. All three are scope holds.
observations.cartographic_credit_observed: The digital topographic base credits the CanVec+ data model, Natural Resources Canada for hydrographic features, and the Manitoba Land Initiative, Manitoba Environment, Climate and Parks.

complete_feature_observations.independent_observation: Highrock Lake and Nelson Lake are distinct directly supported associations in the central/southern and eastern portions of one 115-position ring. The narrow northern arm and intervening reaches include water and mapped land; its proximity to the Suwannee Lake text does not establish a Suwannee component or exact name assignment. Western Highrock bays and detailed southern/eastern continuations are outside the selected ring. Non-exhaustive compound scope hold.

Sisipuk Lake is directly supported for the Manitoba/eastern selected water. The selected western portion crosses the provincial border, outside Manitoba-map hydrographic coverage. The complementary WSA map shows a branching western water footprint but no selected water-name label, and its eastern region is blank. Sandy Bay is a settlement. The two source footprints do not establish a whole-ring named identity or exact cross-border named extent. Unresolved scope hold; no access failure.

Granville Lake is directly supported for the main selected basin, western lobes and northeastern arm toward the separate Leaf Rapids settlement. The narrow southern selected prong follows the Laurie-labelled corridor; the distinct Costello Lake basin is east of that prong. No exact southern-prong named-water assignment is established and no Costello component is warranted by proximity. Chicken Lake is separate northwestern context. Conservative unresolved scope hold for the southern-prong/name transition, with detailed shorelines generalized.
